newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trades record volume as near months rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trades record volume as near months rally.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract traded 490 lots on Tuesday, including 370 lots in the two-hour afternoon session as the exchange recorded its busiest day yet.

Both March and April were firmer, settling up by 0.65 pence and 0.05 pence a therm on Monday's close respectively, while May, June, July and August all slipped. There was no trade in the contracts from September through to February 1998.

"The usual parties were involved, and the market's still very flat, although March and April picked up a bit," said a broker. "There's just a bit more enthusiasm, more people are getting involved, people are getting more confident. It looks like a market which is beginning to work."
A spokeswoman for the IPE said the extra volume was explained partly by the arrival of several new players in the market.
A broker said the contract had always been expected to start relatively slowly.

"Nobody was under the impression that it was going to be all guns blazing. The IPE didn't want that, it just wanted to secure the market," he said. "If it can average 500 lots a day, that'll be great."
